intro: 1.7.1 brings much of what you asked for since 1.7: your streak at the top of every tab, a reading room on a stage, the people you pray for inside your prayers, a You tab built around what you keep, and every quotation with its source.

sections.heading: Your streak, in view
sections.body: A flame and your count now sit beside Premium on every tab, and a tap opens your streak. The flame grows the longer you keep it: Spark from the first day, Candle at seven days, Lamp at forty, Crown at a hundred, and All flame at a year. The last is named after Abba Joseph of Panephysis, who in the Sayings of the Desert Fathers told a brother that he could become all flame. Your badges stay yours for good.

sections.heading: A reading room on a stage
sections.body: The day's book stands at the top on its own picture, and the room settles in as you scroll. Short reads come first, and New to Orthodoxy comes first if you are new. A row for how you feel opens eight Purify collections, from love and grief to envy and loneliness: passages of Scripture and the Fathers, word for word, each opening where it stands. The covers are posters, with every title whole.

sections.heading: Those I pray for
sections.body: Your living and your departed, and the names you add from the prayer wall, now stand in one list inside your prayers. You choose which prayers carry it: morning, midday, evening, the Hours, Compline or your own rule. A name from the wall stays for a week, or until you mark it prayed. When you ask for prayers, you can now say what for, and it goes with your name into the prayers of everyone who adds you.

sections.heading: Every quotation with its source
sections.body: A saint's words, a Father's comment on a chapter, a council or a line of Scripture now carries its exact place, and a tap opens it there, down to the paragraph. The Fathers' books are cited by their own numbering. Lines we could not trace to a public-domain text have left the page until they can be.

sections.heading: You, and everything else
sections.body: You is rebuilt: pick up where you left off, meet a verse you kept each day, and find everything you have kept by what it is. Highlights come in six colours you can name. The calendar is made for your phone. Learn to Pray shows the Sign of the Cross with a real hand, the walkthrough of Job says who each person is to the Church, and the Verse of the Day comes in Turkish, marked as a machine translation.
